subject.title: [Feature]: Per-binding and per-agent permissionMode for ACP sessions

question: Should OpenClaw add scoped ACP permission defaults to configured bindings and per-agent ACP runtime config, and should that contract use canonical ACP runtimeOptions/permissionProfile or ACPX-specific permissionMode/nonInteractivePermissions fields?
rationale: This changes public config shape and security policy inheritance for ACP sessions, so automation should not choose the authorization model or compatibility behavior without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add canonical scoped permission policy
options.body: Expose a scoped permissionProfile-style contract for bindings and agent ACP runtime config, document precedence over global ACPX defaults, and add tests for fresh and upgraded configs.

options.title: Keep ACPX permissions global
options.body: Close or defer the scoped override request and improve docs/errors so operators know ACP permissionMode remains plugin-wide.

options.title: Defer to ACP runtime RFC
options.body: Hold this issue for the broader ACP-everywhere policy model so sandbox and permission capability decisions land together.

recommendation.title: Add canonical scoped permission policy
recommendation.body: Expose a scoped permissionProfile-style contract for bindings and agent ACP runtime config, document precedence over global ACPX defaults, and add tests for fresh and upgraded configs.

likelyOwner.reason: Their ACP session/runtime history is the closest available implementation ownership signal for the security-sensitive runtime policy boundary.
